Refresh.Title: Update from reference: {name}
Refresh.Hint: {n} entries on the sheet differ from the reference — for example, they lack the “Description” and “System” sections. Check what to update; uncheck anything you edited by hand. Rolls, cost, level and dots don't change; for Merits and Flaws the category (clan traits become “Clan”), clan and source are updated too.
Refresh.UpToDate: The sheet's texts already match the reference.
Refresh.ItemUpToDate: The text already matches the reference.
Refresh.NotFound: The reference has no such entry — it's a custom power or trait.
Refresh.ItemHint: Replace the description with the reference text? Your own edits to the description will be lost; rolls, cost and level don't change.
Refresh.WorldHint: {n} sheets have entries (powers, rituals, traits, Backgrounds) that differ from the reference: old texts without “Description” and “System” sections, former trait categories. Manual edits count as differences too — go sheet by sheet if you have any.
Refresh.WorldSkip: Don't ask until the next version

Provocation.Hint: Frenzy provocation — difficulty from the ghoul and dhampir table (Accursed Heirs, ch. 1).
Provocation.lethal: A bullet, knife or other lethal damage
Provocation.rejection: Cruel rejection by a loved one

Dhampir.RulesHint: Dhampir rules and Bloodrights (Accursed Heirs: Dhampirs)
Dhampir.AddHint: Bloodrights whose required Discipline I you have
Dhampir.NoRights: No Bloodrights yet. One dot at creation, then 5 freebie points or experience (new — 7, then current × 5).
Dhampir.RitualsHint: Wits + Occult, diff. 5 + level; no higher than Dririmancy
Dhampir.DiffByTargetNote: The difficulty depends on the target — adjust it in the dialog.
Dhampir.RitualCost: Almost always one level of lethal damage to yourself: blood for the ritual.
Dhampir.NeedReq: You need a dot of the “{d}” Discipline first.
Dhampir.RareNote: “{name}” is a rare Bloodright: only with the Storyteller's permission and a reason in the story.
Dhampir.RemoveConfirm: Remove the Bloodright “{name}” from the sheet?
Dhampir.GrantedFree: “{name}” granted by the Storyteller without experience.
Dhampir.DrinkHint: Drink a point of vampire vitae: it refills your own blood first, the excess becomes ghoul vitae (Accursed Heirs, ch. 1).
Dhampir.VitaeHint: Ghoul dhampir (“Gast”): while holding vampire vitae, a ghoul with Disciplines up to the donor's Generation limit. Spending uses your own blood first; a point of vitae a month keeps you a ghoul. The stomach holds 2 points, more is an overdose (V20, p. 502).
Dhampir.VitaeCharge: {name} drinks vitae — their own blood is refilled.
Dhampir.VitaeGast: {name} drinks vitae beyond their own pool and becomes a ghoul: ghoul vitae — {n}.
Dhampir.VitaeOver: {name} overdoses on vitae: {n} points beyond their pool (V20, p. 502 — overdose consequences).

Hunter.RulesHint: Hunter: The Reckoning — rules and Edges (compendium)
Hunter.BaseHint: Starting Conviction — {n}: the track returns to it at the start of a new story.
Hunter.PrimaryHint: The creed's primary Virtue: the others can't exceed it.
Hunter.UsedHint: Edges of this Virtue: {used} points of {value}.
Hunter.MadnessHint: Virtue {from} and above — a derangement per dot: {n}.
Hunter.SightHint: A point of Conviction per scene: hidden monsters and the possessed are visible, illusions don't fool you; supernatural fear and control over mind, senses and body don't work.
Hunter.SightOn: {name} spends Conviction: Second Sight and self-possession until the end of the scene.
Hunter.VirtueTestHint: A roll of the primary Virtue against an ancient monster (diff. 6–8, Storyteller's call): failure — for the scene, an ordinary human before it.
Hunter.VirtueTestNote: Willpower can't help this roll. Failure — until the end of the scene the monster is invisible to Second Sight and has power over mind and body.
Hunter.RestoreHint: Start of a new story: Conviction returns to its starting value.
Hunter.AtBase: Conviction is already at least its starting value ({n}).
Hunter.Restored: {name}: Conviction is {n} again — a new story.
Hunter.TradeHint: 10 Conviction — a point of Virtue (primary no lower than the others); the track drops to its starting value.
Hunter.TradeHow: Which Virtue grows? The choice should follow from how the hunter earned the Conviction.
Hunter.NoVirtueRoom: No room to grow: the other Virtues already equal the primary one.
Hunter.Traded: {name} gives all their Conviction to the hunt: {v} — {n}.
Hunter.UseHint: Use the Edge: roll, Conviction cost, risk
Hunter.CostNote: The Edge costs {n} Conviction — deducted on the roll.
Hunter.RiskNote: Once per scene you can risk up to {n} points: a die per point; success — everything staked stays and +1 more, failure — the stake burns, botch — all Conviction burns.
Hunter.ByTargetNote: The difficulty depends on the target — set it yourself.
Hunter.RiskBotch: {name} botched a risked roll — all Conviction burned. The hunter is now just a person with a gun who knows too much.
Hunter.NeedPrev: Requires an Edge of this path at level {n}.
Hunter.NeedCreed: Above the highest Edge of the creed's path ({n}).
Hunter.FifthLevel: Level five Edges are locked: the world setting “Hunter: level five Edges” unlocks them (Players Guide, ch. 2).
Hunter.FifthOnce: A hunter can have only one level five Edge.
Hunter.FifthWill: Permanent Willpower of at least 6 is required: the rite takes 5.
Hunter.FifthIntro: “{name}” is power beyond the human. It isn't given: it is sought and accepted by giving up everything that kept the hunter in ordinary life. The price:
Hunter.FifthArch: Nature and Demeanor — Autocrat, Fanatic or Perfectionist;
Hunter.FifthFrozen: the other Virtues never grow again, under any circumstances;
Hunter.FifthPresence: a frightening presence: with ordinary people and most hunters Social pools are halved (rounded down); doesn't affect imbued with a Virtue of 7+, Hermits and Waywards, and to monsters the hunter still seems an ordinary mortal;
Hunter.FifthPatron: Patron 5: the Messengers barely fall silent, but their messages are twisted and push toward extremes — up to atrocities;

FifthCurse.mercy: once per story the Storyteller secretly tells you that the hunter sees in a real monster something worth saving — at any cost, even comrades' lives;
FifthCurse.vision: once per story the Storyteller secretly tells you that the hunter knows something with absolute certainty — and no argument will change their mind;
FifthCurse.zeal: once per story the Storyteller secretly tells you that the hunter has judged someone a threat to be destroyed at any cost — a monster, a human or another hunter;

Hunter.FifthGuard: neither Willpower nor anyone's supernatural power can lift this: the hunter's mind is protected as if by spending Conviction — but Second Sight still costs a point.
Hunter.FifthDone: {name} accepts the Edge “{edge}” — and stops being who they were. Willpower −5, Patron 5, the other Virtues are frozen.

FifthShort.presence: Social pools halved with people and most hunters
FifthShort.curse: once per story the Storyteller may impose a creed decision

Hunter.FifthWaive: Sacrifice: {pts} advancement points — you can lift up to {n} conditions (check them; 10 points each).
Hunter.BudgetHintXp: growth by experience: the Virtue only limits the highest Edge level, the number of Edges — by experience (creed path — level × 5, other — × 7).
Hunter.LostSanityHint: A Bystander's Conviction is their sanity: it starts at 10 and only goes down. At 3, 2 and 1 — a derangement each, at 0 the mind collapses.

LostWhen.courage: Courage — when the Bystander goes against a monster: attacks, blocks its way, speaks to it. Roll: Wits + Courage, diff. 7.
LostWhen.reason: Reason — when they get irrefutable proof: the teacher is a walking corpse, werewolves exist. Roll: Wits + Reason, diff. 7.
LostWhen.selfControl: Self-Control — when sudden horror strikes: a bloodless corpse, a haunted house. Roll: Wits + Self-Control, diff. 7.

Hunter.LostRollNote: Failure — −1 Conviction; botch — also −1 to this Virtue, panic and flight. The familiar is less frightening — the difficulty can be lowered.
Hunter.LostFail: {name} holds on, but what they saw leaves a scar: Conviction {n}.
Hunter.LostMad: {name}: their mind is cracking — derangements now {n} (or the old ones get worse). Add a derangement to the sheet.
Hunter.LostBroken: {name}: no Conviction left — the mind has collapsed. The character passes to the Storyteller.
Hunter.LostTradeHint: Once per game session: a point of Virtue for a point of Conviction. The best in a person goes to hold on to the rest.
Hunter.LostTradeHow: Which Virtue pays for a point of Conviction?
Hunter.LostTradeDone: {name} gives up part of themselves to stay sane: {v} −1, Conviction {n}.
Hunter.LostTraded: A Virtue has already been traded for sanity today.
Hunter.LostHardenedHint: A point of Willpower per scene: don't flee the monster and resist control over mind, senses and body. Doesn't cancel the Virtue roll.
Hunter.LostHardenedOn: {name} grits their teeth: until the end of the scene fear and another's will have no power over them (Willpower −1).
Hunter.LostOrdealHint: Perception, diff. 6 — recognize another Bystander or hunter, even from a photo or a voice on the air.
Hunter.LostOrdealNote: Success — the eyes, the voice, the manner show it: this person has seen too.
Hunter.RiskUsed: Conviction has already been risked this scene — not a second time.
Hunter.AdvancedOther: Experienced hunter: Edges of other paths — no higher than level III.
Hunter.TempHint: Temporary Virtue for deeds: 10 — a permanent point.
Hunter.DeedHint: Storyteller: reward a deed with temporary Virtue points (Players Guide, ch. 2).
Hunter.DeedHow: Compassion — Mercy, seeking understanding — Vision, a decisive blow — Zeal. Usually 1–2 points; the same deed isn't rewarded twice.
Hunter.ShiftHint: Two temporary points of the primary Virtue — one of another (needs a reason in play).
Hunter.ShiftHow: Two temporary points of “{v}” turn into one temporary point of another Virtue. The exchange isn't free: what did the hunter understand?
Hunter.ShiftNeed: At least two temporary points of “{v}” are needed.
Hunter.ShiftWhy: A reason is needed: what changed in the hunter's outlook?
Hunter.CashHint: Ten temporary points — a point of permanent Virtue; the temporary track starts from zero.
Hunter.CashNone: No Virtue has ten temporary points and room to grow.
Hunter.SacrificeHint: Give up a dot of the old life for the hunt: Attribute — former × 3 advancement points, Ability — × 2, Background — × 1; each trait once per story.
Hunter.SacHow: The hunter gives up part of who they were: job, friends, habits, looks. The sacrifice must show in their life. A trait already given this story can't be given again.
Hunter.SacNone: Nothing left to give: everything possible has been given this story.
Hunter.SacDone: {name} gives part of themselves to the hunt: {trait} {from} → {to}, +{n} advancement points (total {total}){why}.
Hunter.AdvanceHint: Advancement points: {n}. Primary Virtue — new × 2, others — × 3; 10 points each lift a level five Edge condition.
Hunter.AdvNone: Advancement points ({n}) aren't enough for any Virtue.
Hunter.AdvDone: {name}: the sacrifices weren't in vain — {v} {n} ({left} advancement points left).
Hunter.FreeformNoTake: Edges “from above”: the hunter has no Edges of their own — call for one per scene (Edges tab).
Hunter.CallHint: A point of Conviction and a Virtue roll (diff. 6): an Edge for the scene, no higher than the successes.
Hunter.CallHow: The hunter prays, shouts, clutches a talisman — and hopes for help. A point of Conviction, a Virtue roll (diff. 6): an Edge of a level no higher than the successes, until the end of the scene. Failure — nothing, the point returns, no asking again this scene; botch — the point is lost, the Messengers are silent until the end of the session.
Hunter.CallBudget: the sum of levels of Edges “from above” per story — no more than the Virtue; one Edge per scene.
Hunter.CallFirst: Edges “from above”: call first — only this scene's Edge can be used.
Hunter.CallSession: The Messengers have turned away: calls won't be heard until the end of the session.
Hunter.CallScene: The call wasn't heard: no asking again this scene.
Hunter.CallHave: This scene has already granted the Edge “{edge}”.
Hunter.CallSpent: The Virtues for this story are spent: nothing left to call on.
Hunter.CallBotch: {name} calls out — and the answer is silence, heavy as a verdict. A point of Conviction is lost; the Messengers are silent until the end of the session.
Hunter.CallFail: {name} calls out, but there is no answer. The Conviction point is safe; no asking again this scene.
Hunter.CallGot: {name} receives from above: “{edge}” — until the end of the scene ({n} successes).
Hunter.CallLess: Not what was asked for (“{want}”), but what was given.
Hunter.SwapHint: Storyteller: choose another Edge of the same Virtue, no higher than the successes.
Hunter.BudgetHint: Virtue points given to Edges: an Edge's level — that many points of its Virtue.
Hunter.Barred: {creed} can't have Edges that discern monsters.
Hunter.HermitMadnessShort: For your creed — with an incurable derangement.
Hunter.NeedVision4: Edges of Solitude for other creeds — only with Vision 4 or higher.
Hunter.HermitMadness: {name} takes the Edge of Solitude “{edge}” — the Messengers' noise leaves an incurable derangement: paranoia, megalomania, manic-depression, obsessive aggression, dissociation, agoraphobia, addiction or demophobia (Storyteller's choice).
Hunter.SightAlwaysHint: A Wayward's Second Sight always sees monsters, for free. A point of Conviction — protection of mind and body until the end of the scene.
Hunter.SightGuardOn: {name} spends Conviction: protection of mind and body until the end of the scene (the Wayward sees monsters anyway).

Exorcist.HunterNote: Second Sight and protection — a point per scene
Exorcist.SightHint: A point of Conviction: Second Sight sees the Fallen over the host body (House and visage), and the hunter's mind and body are beyond the Fallen's power until the end of the scene.
Exorcist.SightDemon: {who} sees through the flesh: the body holds {name} — a Fallen, House {house}, visage {visage}.
Exorcist.Title: Faith against the Fallen
Exorcist.BtnHint: Faith against the Fallen: prayers, exorcism, weapons of faith and quests (“Saviors and Destroyers”, core book ch. 9)
Exorcist.HelpersHint: Drag mortals here: their Faith adds up in prayer, their Willpower in the rite.
Exorcist.ImmuneHint: The Fallen's Torment is 3 or lower: prayers and holy things don't touch them.
Exorcist.NoFaithHint: Without True Faith, prayers and blessed items don't work (the field is on the “Biography” tab).

Pray.banishHint: Faith against the Fallen's Willpower (diff. 6): victory — they leave and don't return here for as many hours as their Torment.
Pray.wardHint: Victory — the Fallen won't enter the area (the praying people's total Faith, in square yards) for as many hours as their Torment.
Pray.bindHint: Victory — the Fallen can't move from the spot while the prayer lasts; they can turn and throw things.
Pray.banishDone: {name} is banished and won't return here for {h} h.
Pray.wardDone: Warding: {name} won't enter {area} sq. yards for {h} h.
Pray.bindDone: {name} is bound by prayer — won't move while it lasts.

Exorcist.PrayWon: The prayer is stronger — it takes effect at once.
Exorcist.Immune: {name} doesn't fear prayers: there is too little Torment in them.
Exorcist.NoBody: {name} has no body right now — nothing to cast out of.
Exorcist.NotOwner: The sheet “{name}” is changed by the GM — the outcome is in chat.
Exorcist.CoreHint: Once an hour — Faith against the Fallen's Willpower. You need more victories than the demon's permanent Faith; then it leaves the body and never returns to it. Without binding the demon simply leaves.
Exorcist.SaviorsHint: First find the host's soul (Perception + Awareness, three tries). Then once an hour — Willpower against Willpower, diff. 8 (with the True Name — 6); the loser loses a point of Willpower. The exorcist's botch ruins the rite forever; the demon's botch or a demon with no Willpower — the spirit goes to the Abyss.
Exorcist.SoulLost: The soul can't be found — the rite can't be performed
Exorcist.FailedHere: The rite over this Fallen has already failed — it can't be repeated.
Exorcist.SoulYes: In the body where {name} lives, the host's soul still glimmers — the rite can begin.
Exorcist.SoulNo: The host's soul doesn't answer — the rite over this Fallen ({name}) can't be performed.
Exorcist.FailedBefore: The rite over “{name}” has already failed.
Exorcist.NoWill: The exorcists have no Willpower left.
Exorcist.Botched: The rite is ruined by a botch — it can never be performed over this Fallen ({name}) again. The shock may leave the exorcists with a derangement.
Exorcist.DemonLoses: The exorcists are stronger ({n} vs {m}): {name} loses a point of Willpower, {w} left.
Exorcist.WeLose: {name} is stronger ({m} vs {n}): each exorcist loses a point of Willpower.
Exorcist.WeBroken: {name} is stronger ({m} vs {n}): the exorcists ran out of Willpower — the rite is lost.
Exorcist.Tie: A tie ({n}) — the hour was wasted.
Exorcist.VictoryAbyss: The Fallen's spirit is torn from the body and goes to the Abyss: {name} is cast out. The host wakes — Willpower 0, a temporary derangement; with each new point of Willpower — a Willpower roll, diff. 7, to get rid of it (botch — forever).
Exorcist.VictoryCore: The exorcism succeeded: {name} leaves the body and never returns to it — they will find a new one or go to the Abyss.
Exorcist.MichaelHint: All spent temporary Willpower returns; no more than once a week (chronicle clock).
Exorcist.MichaelWait: The prayer to St. Michael can be said again from {date}.
Exorcist.MichaelDone: {name} says the prayer to St. Michael the Archangel — Willpower is full ({n}).
Exorcist.MedallionHint: A point of Willpower — until the end of the scene Revelation and mind-controlling evocations don't work. Doesn't protect from wounds.
Exorcist.MedallionOn: {name} clutches the medal of St. Benedict: until the end of the scene neither Revelation nor mind control can take them.
Exorcist.KilaHint: Strike — Dexterity + Melee, diff. 8, damage Strength + 1, lethal. A hit on a Fallen — a Willpower roll, diff. 7: each success removes a point of their temporary Faith.
Exorcist.KilaHit: The kila bites into the flesh — {name} loses {n} Faith.
Exorcist.ZarHint: 12 hours of fasting (Stamina, diff. 6/7/8) and 12 hours of dance (Stamina + Athletics, diff. 7/8/9). Afterwards — 12 chronicle hours: kill the body and the demon goes to the Abyss.
Exorcist.ZarWill: Couldn't endure the fast. Spend a point of Willpower and continue?
Exorcist.ZarFaint: {name} faints from hunger and sleeplessness — the Zar ritual is ruined.
Exorcist.ZarBroke: {name} couldn't endure the fast — the Zar ritual is interrupted.
Exorcist.ZarHurt: {name} collapses exhausted mid-dance — two levels of bashing; the Zar ritual is interrupted.
Exorcist.ZarStopped: The dance is interrupted — the Zar ritual must start over.
Exorcist.ZarDone: The Zar ritual is complete: until {date} the body's death will send {name} straight to the Abyss.
Exorcist.SearchHint: Every 4 hours of work — Intelligence + Investigation (or Occult); difficulty by sources; a point of Willpower — a sure success; botch — everything found was a lie. Only the GM sees how much is needed.
Exorcist.ResearchWill: Research with a point of Willpower (sure success)
Exorcist.ResearchLost: Research “{name}”: the trail was false — start over.

Ghoulify.Btn: Become a ghoul: the mortal drinks vitae — domitor, blood pool, Potence 1, first step of the blood bond
Ghoulify.Title: A mortal becomes a ghoul
Ghoulify.Hint: The mortal drank Kindred blood (V20, “Ghouls”): vitae pool 1 of 2, Potence 1, first step of a blood bond to the domitor. Attributes, Abilities, Virtues, Humanity, Willpower, Backgrounds and items remain.
Ghoulify.DomitorName: Domitor's name (if not in the world)
Ghoulify.ThrallWarn: This mortal is a Fallen's thrall: on becoming a ghoul they lose the pact, the line leaves the master's sheet.

DRitual.NeedText: {n} succ. on the Ankida's Faith roll (diff. 6, +1 per turn, 5 turns)

Court.Name: Infernal court
Court.Hint: Whose court: the tyrant's city or district (“City of Angels”, ch. 4; Fallen rules, ch. 17).

RankTip.subject: Sworn to the court, seeks the favor of superiors and avoids their wrath.
RankTip.knight: The lowest ruling rank: a neighborhood or a lord's errand, a champion in a noble's retinue.
RankTip.lord: A city or several towns, five ministers; retinue about 5, sworn 10–15.
RankTip.highLord: A region or mid-sized city; retinue 8–10, sworn 15–25.
RankTip.baron: A big city, the title taken by force; retinue about 10, sworn 50–75.
RankTip.duke: A continent. None on Earth yet — all in the Abyss.

MinistryTip.eagles: Watchers: intelligence, surveillance, knowledge. Head — the Most Vigilant Watcher.
MinistryTip.aurochs: Guardians: court security, laws and justice. Head — the Venerable Guardian (Lord Owl).
MinistryTip.lions: Swords: army and strategists. Head — the Lord General (Furious Sword).
MinistryTip.dust: Scouts: the mortal world, media, authorities, new sources of Faith. Head — the Herald of the Fallen Tower.
MinistryTip.dragons: Censors: oversight of ministries and the court. Head — the Lord Inquisitor.

Demon.ThrallDeleteAsk: Remove the thrall “{name}” from the list? The pact is broken — their Faith no longer comes.
Demon.ThrallShare: Share to the demon per day
Demon.ThrallNone: No thralls yet. A pact is a voluntary exchange of a gift for Faith (ch. 9).
Demon.ThrallHint: The demon gets no more than half of the thrall's Faith (rounded up), the rest feeds the gifts. If a sheet is chosen — Willpower and wounds are taken from it.
Demon.ThrallDailyHint: The sum of the thralls' shares: arrives at dawn, at any distance (the “Pacts” button)
Demon.OverdrawHint: Wring the thralls: dice to the evocation, no more than permanent Faith. Each die — a point of the thralls' Willpower; beyond Willpower — aggravated without soak. Botch — minus a point of Faith (ch. 9, p. 252)
Demon.OverdrawSplitHint: Distribute {n} points of Willpower among the thralls. Beyond their Willpower — aggravated wounds.
Demon.OverdrawFaith: — the soul is drained, the thrall's Faith is now {f}
Demon.OverdrawNoList: The thralls (by “Pacts”) lose {n} Willpower together — distribute it yourself.
Demon.OverdrawBotch: Botch: the Fallen loses a point of temporary Faith.
Demon.OverdrawTorment: Abuse of a pact — the Storyteller may add Torment, and the thrall may become a worse source.
Demon.FormNoUpkeep: {n} Faith (reliquary and own pool) are needed to manifest without a host.
Demon.FormManifest: {name} condenses Faith into a body and manifests near the reliquary — {n} Faith per turn.
Demon.FormDissipates: {name}: not enough Faith — the body dissipates, the spirit returns to the reliquary.
Demon.FormLookHint: You choose the image and size. In form, the Fallen's tokens in scenes will wear them; after the form they get the old ones back. Empty and “as is” — the token doesn't change.
Demon.FormUpkeepHint: Out of combat: pay Faith for a turn of hostless form (in combat — automatically at the start of the turn)
Demon.PactExistingBtn: Pact with a Fallen: the mortal becomes a thrall (Damned and Deceived)
Demon.PactExistingHint: The mortal makes a pact and becomes a thrall: Virtues — Conscience, Conviction, Courage; sin — by the permanent Willpower threshold. Up to half the thrall's Faith (rounded up) goes to the master every day, the rest to gifts. Add the gifts' bonuses to the traits yourself.
Demon.PactEditHint: Revise the pact: master, thrall's Faith, share, terms, gifts
Demon.PactSealed: {name} makes a pact with the Fallen {master}.
Demon.PactNoDemons: There are no Fallen in the world — no one to make a pact with.
Demon.PactBreakConfirm: {name} stops being a thrall: the pact line leaves the master's sheet, the gifts fade. Continue?
Demon.PactBroken: {name} no longer serves the Fallen — the gifts fade.
Demon.LogHint: Torment log: what changed it and why
Demon.ThrallSinGateHint: The thrall's sin threshold is their permanent Willpower
Demon.ThrallSinBtnHint: A Virtue roll, diff. 7, without spending Willpower: failure — −1 temporary Willpower, botch — −1 permanent
Demon.ThrallSinHint: The thrall's sin threshold is their permanent Willpower ({n}): {sin} The roll is without spending Willpower.

ThrallSinWhen.conscience: innocents were hurt — a car stolen through a gift, a murder on orders
ThrallSinWhen.selfControl: betrayed their principles without harming others
ThrallSinWhen.courage: didn't dare contradict the master or chickened out when others were suffering

ThrallSinRow.10: any cruelty, selfishness, frivolity — and inaction in their face.
ThrallSinRow.9: harming any living being without self-defense or a good purpose.
ThrallSinRow.8: harming a person without self-defense or a good purpose.
ThrallSinRow.7: theft or deceit without reason, a broken oath.
ThrallSinRow.6: harm through negligence, abandoned duties, betrayal of trust.
ThrallSinRow.5: wanton destruction of others' property, deliberate emotional cruelty.
ThrallSinRow.4: sin in passion: murder in anger, hatred, self-destruction.

Demon.ThrallSinOutOk: The thrall finds an excuse — no consequences.
Demon.ThrallSinOutBotch: The sin breaks the thrall: −1 permanent Willpower.
Demon.ThrallSinTemp: {name}: the sin weighs on them — −1 temporary Willpower.
Demon.ThrallSinPerm: {name}: the sin has cracked their will — permanent Willpower {n}.
Demon.ThrallSinMad: {name}: permanent Willpower {n} — a temporary derangement joins the sin (Storyteller's choice).
Demon.ThrallSinBroken: {name}: Willpower is broken — the personality is destroyed, no more Faith for the master.
Demon.EarthboundDoom: Torment 10 — forever: no Virtues, no redemption (Earthbound, ch. 3)
Demon.UrgeSplitHint: Distribute each Urge's dots among its Attributes — even above 5. Next time you can do it differently.
Demon.UrgesHint: Instead of Virtues (Earthbound, ch. 3): in a host body or in form, each Urge's dots are distributed among its Attributes, even above 5. Starting Willpower — the sum of the two highest

UrgeTip.flesh: Strength, Dexterity, Stamina: to eat, to run, to cause pain
UrgeTip.thought: Perception, Intelligence, Wits: curiosity up to vivisection (the first hour in a body — Perception, not Wits)
UrgeTip.emotion: Appearance, Manipulation, Charisma: to feel and break others' passions

ReliquaryHint.ideal: Ideal: soaks damage automatically with permanent Willpower, levels — by Faith, repair 1 Faith per week, hostless form — 2 Faith per turn
ReliquaryHint.improvised: Improvised: soak — a temporary Willpower roll, repair 1 Faith per month, “Resources” no higher than •••, form — 1 Faith per turn
ReliquaryHint.natural: Natural object: soak with permanent Willpower, levels — 2 × (Willpower + Faith), repair 1 Faith per week, omniscience within its bounds, but can't be carried

Demon.ReliquaryDrawTip: Move a point of Faith from the reliquary to your pool (the reliquary's Faith is spent first)
Demon.WorshipTip: The worship ritual is complete: +{n} Faith to the reliquary (by the “Worship” Background; how often — by “Cult”)
Demon.NoWorship: No “Worship” Background — the cult can't give Faith.
Demon.DarkLores: Dark Lores of the Earthbound (10 XP, +1 Torment per use)
Demon.EarthboundTip: Earthbound: Dark Lores and Earthbound rituals without Torment, experience by its own table. Rules — the “Fallen rules” compendium, chapter 13
Demon.AddHouseLoresHint: Add a dot in each Lore of your House
Demon.NoLores: No Lores yet. Choose a House in the header and add House Lores.
Demon.TormentTempHint: Temporary Torment: ten boxes — a point of permanent Torment, the boxes are cleared

Creator.VirtueHintLost: Seven dots among Courage, Reason and Self-Control, each from 1 to 5; with freebie points — 2 per dot.
Creator.ConceptHintLost: The Bystander saw a monster but didn't answer the Messengers. Who are they: family, work, friends, faith — everything they hold on to so as not to go mad.
Creator.AdvHintLost: Five dots of Backgrounds — without Destiny and Patron; Archive and Steel Nerves are available. Seven dots of Bystander Virtues.

Creator.HunterExtra: Experienced hunter: Virtue points beyond three

Creator.HunterConvWill: Starting Conviction no higher than Willpower.
Creator.HunterMadnessHint: An experienced hunter's high Virtue: replace with a derangement from the library that fits their past.
Creator.HunterPrimary: {v} is higher than the creed's primary Virtue ({p}).
Creator.HunterNoBuy: Hunter Virtues aren't bought, Conviction — only with freebie points (no higher than 8).
Creator.ConceptHintHunter: Who this person was before hearing the Message, and how they answered the monster. The creed is their role in the hunt: primary Virtue, starting Conviction and path of Edges.
Creator.AdvHintHunter: Five dots of Backgrounds — general and hunter ones (Arsenal, Bystanders, Destiny…); three points of hunter Virtues.
Creator.BloodrightsHint: Bloodrights — dhampirs only: one dot free (Antiquity 3–4 — two, 5 — three), each further one — 5 freebie points; no higher than 3. Rights that develop a Discipline require its first dot. On top — the Antecedent clan's favored rights.
Creator.BloodrightReq: “{name}”: a dot of the “{d}” Discipline is needed.
Creator.BloodrightMax: “{name}”: there are never more than 3 dots.
Creator.DhSwap: An Antecedent clan Discipline instead of Potence
Creator.DhSwapHint: Accursed Heirs, ch. 3: a clan dhampir can, at creation, replace the free Potence dot with a dot of one of the Antecedent clan's Disciplines.
Creator.DhSwapNeedsClan: Potence is replaced — a dot of an Antecedent clan Discipline is needed.
Creator.EdgesHint: Edges cost Virtue points: an Edge's level costs that many points of its Virtue. Paths — in order; Edges of other paths no higher than the highest Edge of the creed's path.
Creator.FreeHintHunter: 21 points: Attribute 5, Ability 2, Background 1, Willpower 1, Conviction 1 (no higher than 8). Virtues and Edges aren't bought.
Creator.FinishHintHunter: Check the creed, Virtues and Edges. A hunter's Willpower — 3 plus freebie points; the imbued have no Humanity.
Creator.GateHintHunter: The hunter isn't created yet: go through the wizard — creed, traits, hunter Virtues and Edges.
Creator.Title: Creation wizard
Creator.GateHint: The wizard walks you through V20 rules: concept, clan and Generation, Attributes 7/5/3, Abilities 13/9/5, Disciplines, Backgrounds, Virtues, Merits and freebie points — with hints and point tallies.
Creator.PathWill: A follower of a Path needs Willpower of at least 5 (V20, ch. 7).
Creator.DarkFreeOnly: Dark Lores — only with freebie points (5 per dot) or experience.
Creator.WorshipNeedsCult: Worship is impossible without a Cult: Cult • at least is needed.
Creator.ReliquaryHint: The Earthbound's reliquary (Earthbound, ch. 3): ideal — made by mortals for the demon, improvised — the first thing it clung to, natural object — a grove, a cave, a temple.
Creator.EarthboundOn: A King of Horror in a reliquary: Urges instead of Virtues, Faith accumulates from worship, evocations — high Torment only.
Creator.EarthboundOff: A Fallen long locked in an object or place and twisted by mortal worship (Earthbound, ch. 3). Usually — the Storyteller's antagonist.
Creator.EarthboundHint: Create an Earthbound (Earthbound, ch. 3): Attributes 8/6/4, Abilities 17/12/7, Backgrounds 10, Lores 10, Urges instead of Virtues, Faith 4, Torment 10, 21 freebie points
Creator.NeedVisage: Choose a Visage — the main Lore by which the Fallen assumes apocalyptic form.
Creator.OnlyHouse: At the start, Lores — only of your own House and common ones (Fundament, Humanity); others — with experience.
Creator.HouseHint: House is the Fallen's celestial calling: three House Lores and starting Torment. Visage is the main Lore, the apocalyptic form comes from it. Faction — optional.
Creator.ConceptHintDemon: Who the mortal host was and what the Fallen remembers about themselves. Nature restores Willpower. Starting experience — the Storyteller's call.
Creator.DiscHintDemon: Dots: {n} — into your House's Lores and the common ones (Fundament, Humanity). You can see which evocations each dot opens.
Creator.AdvHintDemon: Check Backgrounds and distribute {bg} dots; Virtues — a dot in each and {virt} more. Willpower = the sum of the two highest Virtues.
Creator.DiscHintEarthbound: Dots: {n} — into your House's Lores and the common ones. Dark Lores (Chaos, Contamination, Violence) — only with freebie points (5 per dot) or experience.
Creator.AdvHintEarthbound: Distribute {bg} Background dots — the Earthbound's own Backgrounds (Cult, Worship, Hoard…); no Contacts, Followers, Mentor, Pacts or Legacy. Urges — a dot in each and {virt} more. Willpower = the sum of the two highest Urges.
Creator.FreeHintEarthbound: 21 freebie points at Earthbound prices: Attribute 6, Ability 2, Lore 5, Background 1, Faith 5, Urge 3, Willpower 1. Right-click — remove a point.
Creator.PactTermsPh: what the thrall must do and what the master doesn't demand
Creator.PactWordsPh: “so that no one dares touch me again”, “heal my sister”…
Creator.PactBoostsHint: Attributes — 2 dots per point of Faith, Abilities — up to 5 dots per point; no higher than 5. Other gifts (healing, innate, form traits, evocations, special House gifts) — in words above and with points per chapter 14.
Creator.PactNoMaster: No Fallen master chosen: the pact won't be written to their sheet.
Creator.PactOver: The gifts exceed the thrall's Faith by {n}.
Creator.PactNoPoints: No more Faith points for gifts.
Creator.PactNoAccess: The pact isn't written to the sheet “{name}” — no permission; ask the Storyteller to add the thrall on the master's “Advantages” tab.
Creator.ThrallOn: A mortal who made a pact with a Fallen (Damned and Deceived, ch. 4): Fallen Virtues, thrall's Faith, last step — the pact and gifts.
Creator.ThrallOff: If the mortal made a deal with a demon — create them as a thrall: their own numbers, Fallen Backgrounds and the “Dance with the Devil” step.
Creator.ConceptHintThrall: The person as they were before the pact: the flaw for which they made the deal should be visible. Nature and Demeanor — any (new ones: Damned Soul, Narcissist, Preacher).
Creator.AdvHintThrall: Check Backgrounds and distribute {bg} dots (no Eminence, Legacy, Pacts, Paragon; Caring Master and Initiation are available). Virtues — a dot each and {virt} more. Willpower = the sum of the two highest Virtues.
Creator.FreeHintThrall: Fifteen freebie points: Attribute 5, Ability 2 (now up to 5), Background 1, Virtue 2, Willpower 1, thrall's Faith 7. Right-click — remove a point.
Creator.PactHint: A pact with a Fallen: choose a master, decide how much of the thrall's Faith goes to them (no more than half, rounded up) — the rest goes to gifts. The thrall asks in words, and the price is in Faith points: Attributes 2 dots for 1, Abilities up to 5 dots for 1.
Creator.FinishHintThrall: Thrall's Faith — 1 (plus freebie points), Torment 0, Willpower — the sum of the two highest Virtues. The thrall's sin is counted by their permanent Willpower. The pact is also written to the master's sheet.
Creator.FinishHintEarthbound: Faith — 4 (plus freebie points), Torment — 10 forever, Willpower — the sum of the two highest Urges, reliquary — as chosen at the House step. Lores are written to the sheet along with evocations.
Creator.FreeHintDemon: Fifteen freebie points at Demon: The Fallen prices. Right-click — remove a point.
Creator.FinishHintDemon: Faith — 3 (plus freebie points), Torment — by House, Willpower — the sum of the two highest Virtues. Lores are written to the sheet along with evocations.
Creator.FactionHint: A faction is optional: you can stay apart from all of them.
Creator.FreeCostsDemon: Prices: Attribute {attr}, Ability {abil}, Lore {disc}, Background {bg}, Virtue {virt}, Faith {mor}, Willpower {will}. Right-click — remove.
Creator.XpCostsDemon: Experience per ch. 6: new Lore 7 (other House 10), Lore × 5, Faith × 7. The next dot's price is in the “+” tooltip.

Creator.XpDemon: The Fallen have no age in the Blood: experience beyond creation, if the Storyteller gives it — enter a number.

Creator.GateHintGhoul: The wizard walks you through V20 ghoul rules: concept and domitor, Attributes 6/4/3, Abilities 11/7/4, Disciplines (Potence — from the start), Backgrounds, Virtues, Merits and freebie points — with hints and point tallies.
Creator.GateHintDemon: The wizard walks you through Demon: The Fallen rules: concept, House and Visage, Attributes 7/5/3, Abilities 13/9/5, Lores, Backgrounds, Virtues, Merits and freebie points — with hints and tallies.

Creator.ConceptPh: a Jacobin, a seamstress, a former abbot…
Creator.PathRules: At the start a Path is no higher than 5, Willpower no lower than 5, inhuman Virtues start at 0
Creator.AttrHint: Choose the group priority ({a} / {b} / {c}) and distribute dots. Each Attribute already has one dot.
Creator.AbilHint: Group priority ({a} / {b} / {c}); no higher than 3 at this step.
Creator.GhoulDisc: Potence 1 — free; one more dot of any Discipline.
Creator.GenerationHint: The “Generation” Background: each dot — one generation older than the 13th.
Creator.VirtueHint: Conscience and Self-Control start at 1 (on Paths — 0), Courage — at 1.
Creator.MeritHint: Merits cost freebie points, Flaws give them — no more than 7.
Creator.FreeCosts: Prices: Attribute {attr}, Ability {abil}, Discipline {disc}, Background {bg}, Virtue {virt}, morality {mor}, Willpower {will}. Right-click — remove.

Creator.MageHint: Faction — a Tradition, a Technocratic Convention or a Craft; the Avatar's Essence; one affinity Sphere (from the faction's list). Below is the focus: what the mage believes and how they work magick.
Creator.DiscHintMage: Spheres: {n} dots. One must go to the affinity Sphere. No Sphere may exceed Arete (1 at creation, up to 3 with freebies).
Creator.AdvHintMage: Backgrounds: {bg} dots. Avatar sets starting Quintessence. Mages have no Virtues — on the right is what they start with.
Creator.FreeHintMage: 15 freebie points: Attribute 5, Ability 2, Background 1, Sphere 7, Arete 4 (up to 3), Willpower 1. Raise Arete if the Spheres need room.

TierMage.fledglingHint: Newly Awakened: by-the-book creation, no experience.
TierMage.neonateHint: A few years of study under a mentor: +35 experience.
TierMage.ancillaHint: Decades of the Art, enemies and debts of one's own: +120 experience.
TierMage.elderHint: A century on the Path, a name in the Tradition's chronicles: +300 experience.

MonthlyIncome.Name: Monthly income from Resources
MonthlyIncome.Hint: When the chronicle month changes, player characters with “Resources” get income into their purse, as a single chat card (system rule: in V20 the amount is agreed with the Storyteller).

IncomeTable.Name: Income from Resources by dots
IncomeTable.Hint: Five monthly amounts separated by “/” in the chronicle's currency, for 1–5 dots. Empty — the default: $500/1200/3000/9000/30000 (Revised), 25/100/400/1500/6000 livres in 1789.

HerdNightly.Name: Blood from Herd every night
HerdNightly.Hint: With the “Night” button a vampire with Herd gets as much blood as Herd dots (system rule). Unchecked, Herd, as in the book, only adds dice to hunting.

UiSounds.Name: Interface sounds
UiSounds.Hint: A button click, a drip and a heartbeat when spending blood, a thud on damage, a success bell and a failure tone after a roll. Only for you; volume follows Foundry's “Interface”.

UiSoundVolume.Name: Interface sound volume
UiSoundVolume.Hint: A share of the “Interface” volume in Foundry's sound settings.

DarkAges.Name: Dark Ages content
DarkAges.Hint: Show Dark Ages paths, rituals, Merits and Flaws (V20 Dark Ages, Tome of Secrets, Dark Ages: Vampire 2002 and others) in the creation wizard, library and on the sheet. Independent of the chronicle's era.

Era.Name: Chronicle era
Era.Hint: Changes three Abilities: Drive → Ride, Computer → Theology, Technology → Warfare (system rule).

NightlyWillpower.Name: Willpower on awakening
NightlyWillpower.Hint: The “Awakening” button restores 1 point of Willpower (V20 variant, ch. 5).

DawnWarnings.Name: Dawn warnings
DawnWarnings.Hint: 30 minutes before sunrise and at sunrise — a chat card and a bell for everyone (by the night clock).

UiSkin.Name: “Masquerade” interface skin
UiSkin.Hint: Parchment, cockades and night blue for the sidebar and chat.

ExorcismRule.Name: Exorcism system
ExorcismRule.Hint: How mortals cast the Fallen out of bodies. “Saviors and Destroyers” — finding the host's soul, then hour by hour Willpower against Willpower; victory sends the spirit to the Abyss. “Core book” (ch. 9, p. 256) — Faith against Willpower once an hour, more victories than the demon's permanent Faith; the cast-out one seeks a new body.

HunterGrowth.Name: Hunter: growth of Virtues and Edges
HunterGrowth.Hint: “By the book” — a Virtue grows for 10 Conviction, Edges are granted by Virtue points. “By deeds” (Players Guide, ch. 2) — the Storyteller rewards actions with temporary Virtue points, 10 temporary — a permanent point, Conviction isn't traded for Virtues. “By experience” (Players Guide, ch. 2) — experience buys starting Conviction (new × 5, no higher than Willpower), the primary Virtue (new × 3), others (new × 5), Edges of the creed's path (level × 5) and other paths (level × 7); the Virtue only limits the highest Edge level, there's no 10-Conviction trade.

HunterSacrifice.Name: Hunter: Sacrifice
HunterSacrifice.Hint: Players Guide, ch. 2: the hunter gives up a dot of an Attribute (former × 3 advancement points), Ability (× 2) or Background (× 1), each trait once per story. Advancement points raise Virtues (primary — new × 2, others — × 3), 10 each lift a level five Edge condition; derangements — from Virtue 9, not 7.

HunterFreeform.Name: Hunter: Edges “from above”
HunterFreeform.Hint: Players Guide, ch. 2: the hunter has no Edges of their own. A point of Conviction and a Virtue roll (diff. 6) — an Edge for the scene no higher than the successes (the Storyteller may substitute). Failure — not again this scene, botch — not again this session. The sum of levels per story no more than the Virtue. Reset by the “End of scene” and “End of story” buttons.

HunterEdgeCost.Name: Hunter: Edge cost
HunterEdgeCost.Hint: How many Virtue points an Edge level costs. “By the book” — 1/2/3/4: 10 points take a path up to level IV. “Simplified” (Players Guide, ch. 2) — 1/1/2/2/4: 10 points — up to V, and Edges come sooner (Zeal 4 — already level III).

HunterFifth.Name: Hunter: level five Edges
HunterFifth.Hint: Players Guide, ch. 2: a hunter with a Virtue of 10 can accept one level five Edge. The price — Willpower −5, Nature and Demeanor — Autocrat, Fanatic or Perfectionist, the other Virtues freeze, Patron 5, a frightening presence and once per story — an imposed creed decision.

TormentRule.Name: High-Torment evocations
TormentRule.Hint: How the high-Torment effect of Fallen evocations is decided. “Torment die” — a separate die against permanent Torment (Russian edition of the core book, p. 167). “Majority of successes” — Demon Players Guide errata (p. 17): ones cancel the highest successes, the majority among the rest decides, a tie — the normal effect.

PauseLook.Name: Pause look
PauseLook.Hint: “Drop” — a drop of blood freezes mid-fall, the world fades; on unpause it falls into a puddle. “Foundry default” — the usual caption.

NexusNav.Name: Scene nexus instead of the navigation bar
NexusNav.Hint: Enabled: Foundry's scene strip is hidden, replaced by a plate with the nexus button, scene name and night clock.

Latitude.Name: Chronicle city latitude
Latitude.Hint: Sunset and sunrise are computed from it. Paris 48.86, Lyon 45.76, Marseille 43.30, London 51.51.

Longitude.Name: Chronicle city longitude
Longitude.Hint: Together with the time zone it shifts noon, and with it sunset and sunrise. Paris 2.35, Lyon 4.84, London −0.13.

UtcOffset.Name: City time zone (UTC±)
UtcOffset.Hint: Local time offset from UTC in hours: Paris 1 (local solar time of 1789 ≈ 0.16), London 0.

Currency.Name: Chronicle currency
Currency.Hint: What characters' purses count in. “By era” — livres in 1789, dollars in modern nights; a character can have their own.

AssignatRate.Name: Assignat rate
AssignatRate.Hint: What percent of face value paper assignats fetch in coin right now. The books give no rate — the Storyteller changes it as the chronicle goes.

HuntersAlert.Name: Hunters on Masquerade Exposure
HuntersAlert.Hint: When the city's Masquerade heat reaches exposure, the Storyteller gets a card at nightfall: assemble a hunter cell, place a mark or dismiss it.

InitEachTurn.Name: Initiative every turn
InitEachTurn.Hint: At the start of each combat turn everyone rolls initiative again (1d10 + Dexterity + Wits − wounds), as in V20; one card with the order.

InitFixed.Name: Quick initiative without a roll
InitFixed.Hint: 6 instead of the die: initiative = 6 + Dexterity + Wits (quick variant of the rules).

Declare.Name: Declaration phase
Declare.Hint: After initiative, fighters declare actions from lowest initiative to highest; those delaying act at the end of the turn; defending without a declaration means aborting an action (Willpower).

MageWeekly.Name: Mages: weekly tick
MageWeekly.Hint: As the chronicle clock runs, once a week a cabal's Node yields into the chantry stock, and a mage with Paradox below 5 who cast nothing for a week sheds a point of Paradox.

Combat.FoesHint: Outnumbered: +1 to attack and defense difficulty for each melee opponent after the first, no more than +4.

Combat.AutoHit: The target is fully immobilized — the attack hits automatically.

Hazard.SilverNote: Touching silver deals 1 aggravated per turn of contact; it can't be soaked without a Gift or fetish (put Gift dice in the modifier). Homid and lupus in breed form are unharmed; metis are vulnerable in any form.
Hazard.FireNoteGarou: Fire is always aggravated and ignores armor. Garou soak it with Stamina in any form but their breed form; it repeats every turn until put out.
Hazard.Fireproof: The Visage in assumed form doesn't burn: fire and heat don't wound.
Hazard.FireNoteDemon: Fire wounds a Fallen lethally. They soak lethal damage with Stamina only in apocalyptic form; a Visage with “Resilience” or “Fire immunity” doesn't burn in form.
Hazard.HolyLowTorment: Torment 3 or lower: holy things don't wound the Fallen (ch. 9).

Hazard.HolyRelicLbl: Faith of the object (damage per turn)
Hazard.HolyGroundNote: Old churches and places of living faith. At Torment 4+ — lethal wounds by the place's Faith every turn (the flesh withers, stigmata), and a Willpower roll to stay (ch. 9, p. 255).
Hazard.HolyRelicNote: A consecrated or blessed object pressed to the skin: at Torment 4+ — lethal wounds by its Faith every turn (ch. 9, p. 256).

Hazard.FallNote: 1 die for every full 3 m, bashing damage. From 30 m — 10 dice of lethal, armor counts half.
Hazard.ShockNote: Lethal every turn while in contact; a botched soak — aggravated. Breaking away — Strength, diff. {n}.

Rule.discipline: A new Discipline — 10 XP (for a ghoul — 20), clan ones are highlighted. The first dot opens a level I power; for Thaumaturgy and Necromancy the primary path is chosen right away.
Rule.path: The first path is primary: it grows with the Discipline. A secondary path — 7 XP, its rating no higher than the primary.
Rule.ritual: A ritual's level — no higher than the Discipline's dots. Rituals are obtained through the story — from a mentor or a grimoire — they aren't bought with experience.
Rule.combo: A combination power requires all listed Disciplines at the needed level and a mentor who knows it. The experience cost — by the book (V20 Lore of the Clans and others).
Rule.merit: Merits are taken at creation with freebie points; later — only with the Storyteller's permission.
Rule.flaw: Flaws give freebie points only at creation (no more than 7); later the Storyteller assigns them through the story.
Rule.background: Backgrounds grow through the story and with the Storyteller's permission; dots are chosen with the buttons.
Rule.derangement: A derangement appears over the course of the chronicle — from losing Humanity, Dementation or horror.
Rule.investment: An Investment is a separate deal with a demon: 3 XP (V20, no more than permanent Willpower), sealed with an atrocity and a Humanity roll. Older Investments from the Sabbat books — the Storyteller sets the price. Details — “V20 rules”, chapter 9.
Rule.edge: An Edge costs points of its Virtue by level; path levels — in order; Edges of other paths no higher than the highest Edge of the creed's path. Not bought with experience — they grow with Virtues (Hunter: The Reckoning, ch. 4–5).
Rule.pact: A ready-made pact is a preset: “Take” opens a pact with the gift, price and Devil’s Due rating filled in; enter the demon and the atrocity yourself. The numbers are a guide, the Storyteller adjusts them to the chronicle (reference, sections 9 and 15).
Rule.gift: A Gift no higher than Rank. Your Gifts — from your breed, auspice and tribe lists; others are taught by a spirit through the story (W20, ch. 4). XP: own — level × 3, other — level × 5.
Rule.rite: A rite no higher than the Rituals Ability. Taught by elder Garou and spirits (W20, ch. 4).

Strategy.PerkHint: What influence in the sector gives: dice to a background in downtime, or easier hunting
Strategy.TrendStorm: The trend rages: all bids in this hex at difficulty +1; at level five it erodes the strongest holder.
Strategy.TrendNew: New trend: riot, epidemic, gang war…
Strategy.ProjectNew: New project: found a lodge, install your own mayor…
Strategy.ProjectHint: Start a project in this hex; invest in it with “Invest in a project” bids. The Storyteller sets the track goal (10 by default).

Strategy.OvLead: Hexes on the table: {n}. Click a sphere to highlight its hexes.
Strategy.Contested: Contested hex: the leaders are tied
Strategy.ReadyWait: Still thinking: bids placed, turn not submitted

GarouCr.Title: Garou creation
GarouCr.AttrHint: 7 / 5 / 3 by group — the wizard picks which group gets what, whichever is cheapest
GarouCr.AbilHint: 13 / 9 / 5, at most 3 at creation — higher only with freebies
GarouCr.CostHint: W20 costs: Attribute 5, Ability 2, Background 1, Gift 7, Rage 1, Gnosis 2, Willpower 1. Flaws give points, at most 7.
GarouCr.NeedGifts: Three Gifts are needed: breed, auspice and tribe.
GarouCr.NeedDeformity: A metis needs at least one deformity.
GarouCr.Done: {name}: the Garou is created. Welcome to the Nation.

GarouCr.GiftGeneralFull: You already have {n} general Gifts: drop one to take another.

Sept.Title: Sept

Sept.EmptyGM: Create a sept on the left.
Sept.EmptyPlayer: Your character belongs to no sept.
Sept.TotemRule: A sept totem costs no Background; it can be called once per lunar month; its ban is a principle for the whole sept.
Sept.StandingRule: Standing: • Known, •• Respected, ••• Valued, •••• Honored, ••••• Lauded.

Umbra.Title: Umbra
Umbra.FindHint: Intelligence + Enigmas, diff. 7 — find the way (in the Pattern Web without Web Walker)
Umbra.Pick: Pick a place on the left.

Sins.Ask: Path: {path}, rating {n}. What was done? Sins above {n} (dimmed) need no check.
Sins.Safe: {name}: “{sin}” ({r}) is above rating {n} — no degeneration check.

Group.NoMembers: No one yet — drag characters from the directory.
Group.DropHint: Drag a character in to add a member, a domain to set the Domain.
Group.Primary: Base: no shared Background is higher
Group.RatingHint: Rating works as Domain Background dots: when the owner or their coterie hunts, it lowers the difficulty together with Fame.
Group.HoldingsHint: havens, clubs, businesses, the owner's people
Group.DropMember: Drag a character sheet from the directory here to add them
Group.DropOwner: Drag the owner's sheet — a character or a coterie
Group.DropGuest: Drop a sheet: the owner allowed them to hunt
Group.DropPerson: Drop a sheet: the owner's ghoul, Herd, servant

StatHint.rating: V20: each dot is −1 to hunting difficulty for the owner and guests, +1 blood at the start of play. 1 — a house or business; 3 — a block; 5 — a district, an ethnic enclave.
StatHint.security: V20: each dot is +1 to the difficulty to sneak in and for uninvited vampires to hunt, −1 to find and identify trespassers.
StatHint.prosperity: DA Companion: each dot is −1 to Commerce difficulty; Resources up to this rating cost half the maturation experience.
StatHint.passages: DA Companion: each dot is −1 to difficulty to hide and evade attention for those who know the domain.

Group.StartBlood: Size {n}: +{n} blood at the start of play for the owner
Group.PoolHint: V20: Domain may be shared — both size and security.
Group.PopulaceLine: {h} households (as many militia), ~{p} people, {a} sq. miles
Group.PopulaceNone: Herd may be turned into Population (DA Companion).
Group.ServantsLine: Management and Leadership in domain affairs: difficulty −{n}; up to {k} servants on a journey
Group.ServantsNone: Without servants the estate merely doesn't fall apart.
Group.FeudalHint: DA Companion: for each dot the liege grants a vassal as an anchor, the vassal gives 2; revoking an anchor costs the liege 1 dot. The combined domain is own size plus the vassals'.
Group.HavenNoPool: Add the shared Background Communal Haven in Shares and base — its dots are split here.

curse.name: Curse
curse.text: −1 or more to Herd (Population) or local Resources until lifted; may draw a Saint.

disaster.name: Disaster
disaster.text: −1 or more to Herd (Population), Size or Prosperity; servants restore as many dots as their rating. Unrepaired — Invasion, Brigands, Famine.

saint.name: Saint
saint.text: True Faith, miracles; staying a season or longer — Resources +1 while here. Pilgrims, Heresy.

famine.name: Famine
famine.text: −1 or more to Herd (Population), in time to Servants; Brigands.

invasion.name: Invasion
invasion.text: Mass combat: households are the militia, servants are troops, Allies and vassals other forces. A long war cuts Population, a siege — Size and outside Resources.

court.name: Liege's visit
court.text: Servants at least the liege's Status or Influence; cover the gap with Resources (−1 Resources dot). Failure — punishment, success — Resources, Influence, standing.

heresy.name: Heresy
heresy.text: Gives Influence over its followers but risks excommunication: lost Influence, Kindred Status, Resources.

miracle.name: Miracle
miracle.text: True Faith in a place or object (or a fake): Resources, Influence, Status; Pilgrims, Heresy.

brigands.name: Brigands
brigands.text: Take Prosperity, Resources, Herd (Population); lawlessness hits Influence and Status.

pilgrims.name: Pilgrims
pilgrims.text: One domain Resource +1 while they stay; with hospitality — permanently.

strategy.name: City strategy
strategy.text: A strategy turn shifted the domain's Security: whoever has more tokens in the quarter's sectors (system rule).

trend.name: Trend in the quarter
trend.text: A trend rose on the strategy board in the domain's quarter.

Group.SwayLine: Quarter «{district}»: the owner has {mine} tokens, the rival {best}{who} — at turn end {sway}.
Group.EventTrend: The event became a trend on the strategy board: {name}
Group.TotemPoolNoAccess: The totem's pool is changed by the Storyteller or the pack sheet's owner
Group.TotemBanned: Totem ban broken — no bonuses until the Rite of Contrition
Group.TotemBannedNote: Ban broken: totem bonuses are off until the Rite of Contrition
Group.TotemPoolEmpty: The totem's pool is spent for this story
Group.TotemBanOn: {pack}: ban broken — the totem withdraws all bonuses until the Rite of Contrition
Group.TotemBanOff: {pack}: Rite of Contrition — the totem restores its bonuses
Group.TotemSpendHint: Spend a point instead of your own
Group.TotemRefillHint: The totem's pools refill at the end of each story
Group.TotemAcceptHint: Each Garou of the pack gains temporary Renown from individual traits (once per totem) and Attribute bonuses
Group.ChantryPointsHint: Chantry Background points pooled by the cabal: 10–20 — squat, 21–30 — small sanctum, 31–70 — chantry, 71–100 — fortress, 101+ — seat of power
Group.NodeRateHint: Quintessence a Node dot yields per week: 2 — ordinary world, 5–10 — high magick, 1 — magick is dying (Storyteller's call)
Group.NodeWeekHint: A week has passed: +{free} free Quintessence and +{tass} Tass to the stock
Group.NodeWeekMsg: {name}: the Node gave its weekly yield — free Quintessence +{free}, Tass +{tass}.
Group.NodeNone: The chantry has no Node — no yield.
Group.NodeDrawHint: Draw a point from the chantry stock (free Quintessence first, then Tass)
Group.LibraryHint: shared Background: the chantry's books and archives

Session.Title: Session panel
Session.ToToken: To the token on its scene

Degen.Botch: Botch: {virtue} −1 (now {n}) and a derangement — chosen by player and Storyteller.
Degen.Beast: Morality at zero — the Beast has won: the character goes to the Storyteller.

Instinct.Lead: Instinct {n}: no roll to resist — the character frenzies. If the provocation's difficulty is below Instinct, they may choose not to.
Instinct.CanResist: Provocation {d} is below Instinct {n} — the frenzy may be refused.
Instinct.NoResist: Provocation {d} is not below Instinct {n} — frenzy is unavoidable.
Instinct.Resisted: {name} accepts the Beast and holds it back: provocation {d} is below Instinct {n}.
Instinct.Frenzied: {name} frenzies (provocation {d}). To act consciously — “ride the wave”: an Instinct roll.
Instinct.RideNote: In frenzy: success — a conscious action, the frenzy goes on

PathShift.Btn: Take a Path of Enlightenment (leave Humanity)
PathShift.OnlyHumanity: Only a vampire on Humanity can switch to a Path.
PathShift.Title: Switch to a Path: {name}
PathShift.Lead: Humanity {n}. Required: Humanity 3 or less, replaced Virtues at 1, a mentor of this Path, a year of study and a trial with a monstrous act. Willpower roll, difficulty {d}; Willpower can't buy a success.

Cond.trial: The trial passed — the monstrous act understood

PathShift.RollNote: Success — Path 1 (3+ successes — Path 2), new Virtues at 1
PathShift.Fail: {name} commits a senseless atrocity, but the Path doesn't open: Humanity {n}. May try again in a month.
PathShift.Botch: {name}: botch — the Path is closed, may try again only in a year.

Embrace.Btn: Embrace: a mortal or ghoul becomes Kindred — clan and generation from the sire, first step of the bond
Embrace.Title: Embrace: {name}
Embrace.Hint: A Kindred drains and feeds their blood (V20, ch. 6): clan from the sire, generation is sire's + 1, the childe is bound to the sire at the first step. Attributes, Abilities, Virtues, Humanity, Willpower, Backgrounds and items stay; clan Disciplines are added at 0 dots.
Embrace.SireName: Sire's name (if not in the world)
Embrace.NoInert: Angra Mainyu cannot Embrace: their blood is inert.
Embrace.NoDies: Blood Brothers cannot Embrace: the mortal dies.
Embrace.DoneBond: First step of the blood bond to the sire ({sire}).

Vessel.Label: Vessel
Vessel.Rich: Werewolf blood is potent: more than 3 points may be drunk per turn.
Vessel.Dose: How much (100 g of spirits / strength)
Vessel.Noticed: {name} notices the disease in the vessel's blood — and does not drink.
Vessel.Carrier: {name} now carries a blood disease: the Disease Carrier flaw is on the sheet.

SubFx.alcohol: −1 die to Dexterity and Intelligence per 100 g, fading by a die per hour.
SubFx.stimulant: Celerity +1 for those who have it for (10 − Stamina) minutes; frenzy checks +1 difficulty.
SubFx.hallucinogen: −1 to −3 dice to all pools; Alertness or Auspex may rise; like Hallucinations for (8 − Stamina) minutes.
SubFx.opiate: −2 dice to Dexterity and all Abilities for (10 − Stamina) minutes; dozing for (12 − Stamina) hours; −1 difficulty against frenzy.
SubFx.marijuana: Time distortion, −1 die to Perception for about 30 minutes.
SubFx.poison: −1 die to all pools; 1–3 lethal per scene or turn by toxicity — the Storyteller; remove the effect once the tainted blood is spent.
SubFx.food: Nausea: cannot drink blood (Stamina diff 6 to override for a while), 1 bashing; about a day.

TP.MarkTarget: Target someone (T) — difficulty is taken from them
TP.NoTarget: No target: difficulty is the victim's {what}, set it manually.
TP.DomGeneration: “{name}” is of lower generation: Dominate cannot affect stronger blood

Note.Dom1: A one-word command; cannot order self-harm.
Note.Cond: Extended: one roll per scene, the Storyteller knows the required successes.
Note.Insane: A botch turns the madness on the vampire.
Note.Tele: Reading a vampire's or other supernatural mind costs 1 Willpower.

Tier.Mes1: 1–2 successes: only what doesn't seem strange to them.
Tier.Mes3: 3–4 successes: obeys unless it obviously threatens their life.
Tier.Mes5: 5+ successes: nearly any command short of self-harm or against Nature.
Tier.Forg1: 1 success: one memory removed for a day.
Tier.Forg2: 2 successes: one memory removed permanently, not replaced.
Tier.Forg4: 4 successes: one scene rewritten or erased.
Tier.Forg5: 5 successes: significant periods of life reconstructed.
Tier.Whis3: 3 successes: lasting help — e.g. watching a place for weeks.
Tier.Burn2: 2 successes: malfunctions — +1 difficulty to use until the end of the scene.
Tier.Burn4: 4 successes: broken; after repair permanently +1 difficulty.

TP.DreadDice: −{n} dice to pools until the end of their next turn
TP.DreadFlee: flees in terror; −{n} dice to pools until the end of their next turn

Dur.scene: until the end of the scene

TP.NeedTarget: Target someone (T): this power needs a target
TP.NotKindred: “{name}” is Kindred: this power does not affect vampires
TP.EyesRoll: “{name}” is supernatural: the Setite needs a Willpower roll, difficulty 9.
TP.EyesMortal: meets the gaze — frozen in place
TP.EyesSuper: frozen by the gaze; if attacked or harmed — 1 Willpower to break free
TP.PoisonNote: {n} blood into venom. Willpower, difficulty 6; successes set the duration. Delivery: skin touch or a melee weapon.
TP.PoisonResisted: the venom had no effect — resistance cancelled every success
TP.PoisonDesc: Stamina −{n} {dur}. At Stamina 0 a mortal is terminally ill, a vampire falls into torpor.
TP.QuellNote: Extended roll: {n} successes needed (“{name}”'s permanent Willpower); a failure resets the total.
TP.QuellDesc: cannot spend or regain Willpower, does not resist mental or physical influence; in mortal danger may break free — extended Willpower (diff. 6) to {n} successes, once a day; remove manually
TP.Beast1: the Beast passes to a random suitable target — the Storyteller chooses who
TP.Beast2: the Beast passes to the chosen target; the vampire loses the next turn or acts at once for 1 Willpower
TP.Beast3: the Beast passes to the chosen target
TP.BeastFail: {name}: the Beast didn't leave — frenzy for twice as long and twice as hard to stop
TP.BeastBotch: {name}: botch — uncontrollable frenzy that Willpower cannot stop
TP.GMOnly: The Storyteller places darkness and tentacles on the scene
TP.NoToken: “{name}” has no token on the scene
TP.ShroudDone: a cloud of darkness {d} m across: everyone inside is blind (+2 difficulty), all light but fire dies, −2 dice to Stamina; mortals — Courage or flee
TP.ArmsDone: tentacles: {n} (Strength {s}, Dexterity {d}); they grab and crush — Strength + 1 lethal; 4 health levels, fire and sunlight hurt them as a vampire
TP.Vanish1: a translucent silhouette: the observer rolls Perception + Awareness (diff. 8), on a failure +2 difficulty to all actions against the vampire
TP.Vanish4: vanished completely — Unseen Presence; with more successes than the observer's Willpower, they forget the vampire was there
TP.GatherNoCloak: Turn on Obfuscate first (Cloak of Shadows, Unseen Presence or Mask of a Thousand Faces)
TP.GatherMark: Target the companions (T) — one per dot of Stealth
TP.GatherDesc: under the vampire's Obfuscate; whoever breaks its conditions is revealed, if the vampire does — everyone is

TasteKind.ghoul: a ghoul's blood — mortal, laced with vitae
TasteKind.werewolf: a werewolf's blood — hot and bestial
TasteKind.demon: a mortal host's blood — with something alien inside

TP.TasteDiab: the blood bears a trace of diablerie
TP.RageEmpty: the target has no blood to spend
TP.RageDesc: spent {n} blood at the thaumaturge's will; +{n} difficulty to resist frenzy until the end of the scene
TP.TheftDone: {n} blood flows to “{name}”; no blood bond forms; in public — a Masquerade breach
TP.PotencyAsk: Successes: {n}. The first — 1 step for 1 hour; each extra — another hour or another step.
TP.PotencyDesc: generation lowered by {s} for {h} h; afterwards excess blood spills out
TP.PotencyOnce: Blood of Potency — no more than once a night
TP.MortalsOnly: “{name}” is not mortal: this power affects mortals only
TP.NotAnimal: “{name}” is not an animal: target an animal
TP.PossessStruggle: loses {n} Willpower, {left} left; the struggle continues with the next roll
TP.PossessNote: Resisted: “{name}” rolls current Willpower, difficulty 7; each extra success costs them a Willpower point. A botch frees the target, immune until the end of the story.
TP.PossessedDesc: the body is held by another mind; Manipulation + Intimidation (diff. 7) sets the depth of control
TP.EmptyBodyDesc: the vampire's spirit is in another body; their own lies inert and helpless
TP.PossessDone: Willpower exhausted — the mind lies open to possession
TP.ProjectDesc: the astral form travels; the body is torpid and perceives nothing; each further scene — a new roll and 1 Willpower

FleshNote.lower: Each success — −1 Appearance. A resisting victim must be grappled.
FleshNote.raise: Each success — +1 Appearance (up to 5). A resisting victim must be grappled.
FleshNote.armor: Each success — +1 soak die at the cost of 1 Strength.

TP.SubsumeDesc: the vampire inhabits the animal, their own body unconscious as in torpor; available: {list}. Acting against its instincts costs Willpower (under 3 successes). Leave — remove this effect
TP.SubsumeBlocked: “{name}” isn't available in the animal body — too few successes on Subsume the Spirit
TP.WhisperNote: Difficulty for “{name}”: {n} (6 — predators, 7 — other mammals and raptors, 8 — birds and reptiles). Natural sounds and poses — −1.
TP.Aura1: aura: brightness and intensity of feeling are visible
TP.Aura2: main colour and dominant feeling — as the Storyteller describes

AuraKind.ghoul: an aura with dull blotches of vitae — a ghoul
AuraKind.werewolf: a vivid, roiling aura — a werewolf
AuraKind.demon: something alien in the aura, unlike any human
AuraKind.spirit: an aura without a body — a spirit
AuraKind.creature: an inhuman aura — a supernatural creature

TP.Aura4: fleeting shades and mixed feelings are visible
TP.AuraDiab: black veins — the mark of diablerie
TP.AuraClean: no trace of diablerie or outside influence
TP.VisageCopyNote: A flawless copy takes 5 successes; fewer leaves visible flaws.
TP.BeckonDone: arriving: {name} ×{n} — no control or commands (use Feral Whispers for that)
TP.HeartlessStake: {name}: there is no heart in the chest — a stake does not paralyze
TP.PathOwnNote: Difficulty from “{name}”: {n} (max 10). Against a vampire — costs Willpower.
TP.Resisted: resisted — the magic had no effect
TP.NoFortitude: Without Fortitude there is no resisting.
TP.ComradesNone: First use a lesser Path of Mars power on yourself
TP.Contra0: the target does worse than intended and notices nothing
TP.Contra2: the target does worse but senses interference
TP.Contra3: the target does worse and knows who interfered
TP.Contra4: the target is confused — does neither
TP.Contra5: the target resists and does what was intended

Limb.leg: leg cramped: +2 difficulty to Dexterity actions (standing, dancing, balance)
Limb.arm: the arm hangs limp and useless
Limb.head: the face twitches, no speech: +2 difficulty to social rolls

TP.CorruptDesc: {what} drops to 1, −1 die to all pools
TP.SplitAsk: Distribute {n} temporary points among Physical Attributes.
TP.SplitDesc: Strength +{s}, Dexterity +{d}, Stamina +{st}; in combat — 1 turn plus a turn per extra success ({n} succ.)
TP.WaterMortal: a mortal's blood turns to water — they die within minutes
TP.WaterVamp: {n} blood turned to water: wound penalty as from that much damage; the water leaves a point an hour
TP.SleepDesc: Sleeps 5–10 hours, without nightmares or derangements; can be woken normally.
TP.DustVamp: pale and gaunt: Appearance −1 until the next night
TP.DehydrateDone: desiccation: {n} — blood first, then unsoakable lethal damage; the target rolls Courage (diff. 3 + extra successes) or loses a turn to pain
TP.Atrophy2: the limb weakens: +1 difficulty to actions with it
TP.Atrophy1: the limb withers: +2 difficulty to actions with it
TP.Atrophy0: the limb is crippled; a vampire heals it for 5 blood, a mortal — never
TP.VinesDone: plants come alive for {n} turn(s) under full control
TP.GiantDone: the tree awakens for {n} turn(s) and obeys spoken orders; immune to bashing, lethal damage pool halved
TP.ElementalDone: the elemental arrives and must at least listen; {n} more trait dots — Storyteller's call; binding — Manipulation + Occult

PathNote.Marionette: the body is in another's power: physical actions with its pools at +2 difficulty; 1 Willpower — a mental or social action
PathNote.Subvert: gives in to suppressed desires; at a good chance — yield or spend 1 Willpower
PathNote.Dissociate: withdraws and suspects everyone: −3 dice to social rolls; refusing to act so — 1 Willpower
PathNote.Addiction: addiction: each night without a “dose” −1 die to all pools (cumulative); refusing — Self-Control (diff. 8)
PathNote.Dependence: away from the thaumaturge −1 die to all pools and no Willpower regained; against their influence the pool is halved
PathNote.Stigma: Manipulation, Charisma and Appearance +1 until sunset (remove manually)
PathNote.Malady: weakness: −1 die per success (up to 3) to Strength, Dexterity, Stamina; may shake it off at night
PathNote.Pariah: everyone sees the target as their worst enemy; Auspex doesn't help
PathNote.Grace: phantom failure: no more than 2 successes on any action, an extra botch die on each
PathNote.Prison: in a water prison: escape — Strength + Potence (diff. 8), more successes than the thaumaturge
PathNote.WarCry: Courage +1; Willpower counts 1 higher against hostile powers
PathNote.StrikeTrue: Strike True: melee hits with 1 success without a roll (if the pool isn't split); defense needs just 1 success too
PathNote.WindDance: dodges any number of attacks per turn without penalty
PathNote.Fearless: Strength, Dexterity, Stamina +1; afterwards 2 hours of rest, or −1 blood every 15 minutes
PathNote.Readiness: a die per success into a special pool for Wits rolls (or +1 initiative per unused die)
PathNote.Centering: pools aren't reduced (wounds, penalties, Disciplines); +2 dice against frenzy
PathNote.OneTrack: can't split pools or change tactics; the declared action −1 difficulty; changing course — 1 Willpower
PathNote.Dual: a second, mental action at the same time as the first
PathNote.Clarity: −2 difficulty to all actions; immune to frenzy and Rötschreck; influencing them — +2 difficulty
PathNote.Slumber: sleeps until the condition is met

TP.CounterNote: Thaumaturgical Countermagic: {n} dice, difficulty 6; each success cancels one success of opposing magic.
TP.ConjureHint: steel club, stake, chunk of granite…
TP.ConjureScene: “{name}” in hand — lasts while 1 Willpower is paid each turn (vanishes at the end of the scene)
TP.ConjureNone: Nothing to make permanent — use Summon the Simple Form first
TP.QuellKindredNote: “{name}” is in frenzy: soothing form, difficulty 7; 3+ successes — the Storyteller may allow a new Self-Control roll.
TP.QuellKindredOk: {by} soothes “{name}”'s Beast: the failed frenzy roll may be retried
TP.QuellImmune: “{name}” is immune to this vampire's Quell the Beast until the end of the scene
TP.BeastOutDesc: leave the scene before the target's frenzy ends and the Beast may stay in it; without the Beast the vampire is apathetic, cannot frenzy, spend or regain Willpower
TP.SubsumeDeath: {beast} dies — {name}'s mind returns to the body and falls into torpor
TP.PresImmune: “{name}” is immune to this Presence power of this vampire
TP.PresImmuneNight: {name}: immune to this vampire's “{power}” until dawn
TP.PresImmuneStory: {name}: immune to this vampire's “{power}” until the end of the story (remove manually)
TP.StillActive: The previous effect still holds on “{name}” — not again until it ends
TP.AweNote: Targets marked: {n}. Reach: 1 success — 1, 2 — 2, 3 — 6, 4 — 20, 5+ — all; the lowest Willpower yield first.
TP.AweDesc: drawn to the vampire, readily agrees; shaking it off — 1 Willpower and Willpower (diff. 8) per scene, after spending {n} Willpower free until the end of the night
TP.CallNote: Summon “{name}”: difficulty {n}; the call lasts until dawn.
TP.Call3: comes without haste, but doesn't dawdle on purpose
TP.Call5: hurries with all their might, short of risking their life
TP.MajestyOk: found the nerve — acts, with a heavy heart (no new roll for the rest of the scene)
TP.MajestyFail: dares not stand against “{name}” — backs down and may grovel for forgiveness
TP.DomImmune: “{name}” is immune to this vampire's Dominate until the end of the story
TP.GhoulNotOwn: “{name}” is another vampire's ghoul: Possession works only on a ghoul who drank your blood
TP.MesWhat: Program (what to do and on what trigger)
TP.MesKept: a stronger program is already in place ({n} succ.) — the new one didn't take
TP.ForgRestore: To restore: Dominate at least {d}, Wits + Empathy (diff. {w}), more than {n} successes.
TP.CondDesc: follows the master's orders literally, even to their own harm; other vampires' Dominate +2 difficulty (max 10); in full isolation it fades — about 6 months minus a week per Willpower dot ({w})

sheet.title: Character sheet
sheet.lead: Everything about the character on one page; tabs on the left.

1.d: Click an Attribute or Ability name to open the roll window: second trait, difficulty, Willpower, specialty are there.

2.d: Dots are clicked only during creation; afterwards growth goes through the Experience window (button at the bottom).

3.d: At the top: spend blood by clicking a drop, Willpower with “Spend”, damage and healing by the health track. Wound penalties apply to rolls automatically.

4.d: Disciplines tab: expand a Discipline and click the die by a power. The icon next to it toggles effect powers.

5.d: Effects tab — everything active now: powers, conditions, poisons, curses. An effect can be removed there too.

6.d: The (i) button in a window header shows and hides short explanations inside that window.

hud.title: HUD
hud.lead: The panel at the bottom for the selected token — the essentials without opening the sheet.

1.d: Fight, Blood, Powers, Other — above the portrait. Select your token and the HUD shows it.

2.d: Powers tab: a Discipline icon opens its powers, click a power to roll or toggle it.

3.d: Weapons, maneuvers, “…” — the full attack window; dodge, block, parry — answering an attack. During declarations “Declare” comes first.

4.d: Spending blood, healing, Potence and Celerity extra actions for this turn.

5.d: Powers against a target take difficulty from the marked token: hover it and press T.

turn.title: Combat turn
turn.lead: Three phases per V20: initiative, declarations, actions.

1.d: Rolled every turn: 1d10 + Dexterity + Wits − wounds. The order card goes to chat. Ties — higher initiative rating.

2.d: From lowest initiative to highest. On your turn — a bell and a notice; “Declare” in the tracker or the HUD.

3.d: Declare “Multiple actions” — roll and attack windows split the pool themselves.

4.d: Declaring “Delay” — the character acts at the end of the turn.

5.d: If something else was declared, defending aborts it: a Willpower roll (diff. 6) or 1 Willpower. The system asks.

6.d: Extra actions come in a phase after everyone: the window shows how many are left and offers attack, a roll or movement.

fight.title: Attack and defense
fight.lead: Attack — defense — damage — soak: all through chat cards.

1.d: Mark a target (T) and open the attack: weapon or maneuver, aim, position. Nearby foes and firearm range fill in themselves.

2.d: The attack card has defense buttons for the target. Each further defense in a turn — one die less.

3.d: After a hit — the damage button, then the target soaks. Wounds go to the track automatically.

4.d: They last between turns: in a clinch both take Strength damage each turn. Break free — the HUD button (contested Strength + Brawl).

5.d: Fire or sunlight damage to a vampire — the system offers a Rötschreck check.

6.d: A mortal with a full track, a vampire in torpor or staked — marked defeated in the tracker automatically.

powers.title: Powers
powers.lead: Discipline powers 1–5 work per V20 text; choices are buttons.

1.d: Where a power has several modes, the window shows them as buttons with explanations — one click.

2.d: Difficulty comes from the target (Willpower, Courage…), the result is applied with a card button; the target's owner or the Storyteller clicks it.

3.d: If a rule forbids it, the system asks; bending a rule shows up for the Storyteller in chat. Without a target a power can be rolled plainly.

4.d: The “Use” window: blood and Willpower cost from the book (adjustable), a line to chat; a normal roll if needed.

5.d: “Custom work” — weapon, cost, body changes, soak, spikes; save templates under your own name.

6.d: Active powers and those laid on you are on the Effects tab; durations follow the chronicle clock.

blood.title: Blood and healing
blood.lead: Blood is fuel: Disciplines, physical traits, healing.

1.d: How much blood can be spent per turn depends on generation; the system tracks it.

2.d: 1 blood — bashing or lethal, 5 — aggravated. In combat — a choice: only heal this turn, or heal on the move (Stamina + Survival, diff. 8).

3.d: With blood for this turn: Potence — automatic Strength successes, Celerity — extra actions.

4.d: A “Check” card in chat: a Self-Control or Courage roll against the stimulus difficulty.

5.d: In the evening — minus a blood point, boosts reset; the “Awaken” button on the sheet.

chat.title: Chat cards
chat.lead: Every roll is a card: dice, result and what's next.

1.d: The edge color is the outcome: bone — success, brighter — exceptional, grey — failure, blood — botch.

2.d: The card's main action: damage, apply a power, take damage, roll a check.

3.d: Buttons on a target are clicked by its owner or the Storyteller; on your own card — by you.

4.d: At the start of a turn — the initiative card and the previous turn's summary: who took what and who is out.

gm.title: For the Storyteller
gm.lead: Time, scenes, experience and extras — from the top plate and the tracker.

1.d: Click the clock — calendar; the hourglass starts a scene (timer) and ends it (“until end of scene” effects are removed).

2.d: The star on the plate — session experience; ghoul retainers get half their domitor's experience automatically.

3.d: “Extras” during declarations — all NPC declarations in one window; the sword on an NPC row — its attack.

4.d: The tracker button ends declarations early; those delaying go to the end of the turn.

5.d: In the system settings: initiative every turn, quick initiative (6 + traits), the declaration phase — can be turned off.

6.d: A blood ring around the token whose turn it is; change it in the combat tracker settings.
